clue.text: With apprehension raised by 1 over 8?

parts.note: 'one over the eight' is an idiom for slightly drunk, and tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone nervous, apparently made so by a cross-reference to the grid's eighth clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 and 8 look like references to other clues, but read them as words: 'one over the eight' is an old British phrase for having had a drink too many.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight is informal for tense and anxious, a state full of nervous worry.

clue.text: Dismantle international selection?

parts.note: the United Nations, an international body
a pick is a choice or selection

explanation.surface: A question about taking apart some worldwide choice.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpick is to undo stitches or take something apart piece by piece.

clue.text: Subtitle of 25, then we turn into a green mess

indicators.note: to turn the little word we round is to flip its two letters about
a mess is a jumble, so the words before it are muddled up

parts.note: all ten letters used as written

explanation.surface: A recipe for turning something into a green mess, framed as a book's subtitle.
explanation.walkthrough: Disraeli's novel Coningsby (25 across) is subtitled The New Generation. 'into' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Coningsby's full title is Coningsby, or The New Generation, so this phrase is that book's secondary title.

clue.text: See 2
Headpiece for "Island in the Sun"? On the contrary, quite the reverse

indicators.note: reverse here means the whole result is then read from back to front
swaps the quoted phrase round, so the sun goes inside the island rather than the island inside the sun

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A headpiece costume for a performance of the song Island in the Sun.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the sun god in the island to get A-RA-IT, then reverse it all. Island in the Sun is a Harry Belafonte song.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled coronet worn on the head, so it is a piece of headwear.

clue.text: Queen Bee (in the old poet) seems to be optimistic at the bridge table

definitions.text: be optimistic at the bridge table

indicators.note: the royal insect pair is placed inside the name of the classical poet

explanation.surface: A queen bee hiding inside an ancient poet seems hopeful at a game of bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To overbid at bridge is to bid more than your hand can make, an optimistic contract.

clue.text: 8's style of his party producing anteversion in a vegetable

indicators.note: the rearranged word sits inside the vegetable

parts.note: split as ante plus version: the second half signals a rearranged rendering of the first

explanation.surface: Anteversion is a medical word for tilting forward, so this sounds like a deformed vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: Split anteversion into 'ante' and 'version'. One-nation Conservatism is the paternalist Tory tradition traced to Disraeli (8).
explanation.definitionFit: One Nation is the name for Disraeli's brand of Toryism, uniting rich and poor.

clue.text: Bird of the wilderness

indicators.note: the answer is made of part of the following word, lying within it

parts.note: found in the middle of the last word

explanation.surface: A wild bird living out in the wilds.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a crossword favourite among birds.

clue.text: Premier associated with Primrose Hill: a jailer confused when intelligence is imprisoned

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain or hill

indicators.note: a prisoner is held inside, so the intelligence goes within the jumble
confused letters are jumbled, so the jailer phrase is mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, joining the jumble

explanation.surface: Primrose Hill is a London park; a muddled warder has his wits locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primrose Hill' looks like one place, but the Hill is split off. Disraeli's favourite flower was said to be the primrose; the Primrose League was founded in his memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Disraeli was twice Prime Minister, and Primrose Day and the Primrose League commemorate him.

clue.text: See 7
Song of praise composed by an ape …

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A hymn of praise written by a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A paean is a hymn or song of triumph and thanksgiving.

clue.text: … which has 9s (with a stammer) in range

parts.note: refers back to the animal in the previous clue
9s are nines, and a stammer repeats the first letter

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the ape sings hymns, stuttering, across a range.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9 is not the answer to 9 across but the plain number nine; 'which' points back to the ape at the end of the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the mountain range running down the length of Italy.

clue.text: One organ did another's job in the human body — removes from table

indicators.note: the organ sentence is placed inside the word for the body

parts.note: the body as mortal clay, the stuff of which humans were made
a hearing organ that did the seeing job of the eye

explanation.surface: A medical oddity in which one organ takes over another's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Clay for the human body is a biblical idea: Adam made of dust and clay.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear away is to remove dishes and leftovers after a meal.

clue.text: Strip for footballer that has lost heart

indicators.note: losing heart means dropping the centre letter of the nickname

parts.note: Gazza is the nickname of the English footballer Paul Gascoigne

explanation.surface: A dispirited footballer with a strip, or kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip looks like football kit, but it is the Gaza Strip.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gaza Strip is the narrow Palestinian territory on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Trouble descends upon caricaturist

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or trouble

explanation.surface: Trouble befalls a cartoonist.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Rowlandson was a Georgian English artist famous for satirical caricatures.

clue.text: Make a mistake — I have to — in essay describing an army

indicators.note: the mistake and the rest are set inside the word for an attempt

parts.note: to essay is to attempt, and a trial is an attempt

explanation.surface: A confession that one must make a mistake in writing an essay.
explanation.walkthrough: Essay here is an attempt, not a composition. The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Territorial is the adjective in Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve.

clue.text: Italian river in French city: editor must have it put back

indicators.note: the river flows inside the name of the city

explanation.surface: Geography and editing: an editor restores a river and city reference that was cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimpose is to put a rule or tax back in place after it was lifted.

clue.text: Meal with no starter deleted — that's a blow

indicators.note: no starter means the first letter of the meal is left off

explanation.surface: A dinner whose first course has been axed, which is a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: Starter looks like a first course, which fits the meal, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is a boxing punch swung upward to the chin.

clue.text: Begin to grasp the reel is ready?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for starting to understand
second meaning: thread has been wound on the spool

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: a reel with its thread wound on it has cotton on.
explanation.definitionFit: To cotton on is informal for catching on or realising, and a loaded reel literally carries thread.

clue.text: Designed to advertise a concert, one with no alto playing

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms

indicators.note: playing suggests performing freely, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A concert put on for publicity, with an alto absent from the performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotional material is made to publicise or advertise a product or event.

clue.text: Six strong? That's OK

explanation.surface: A crew of six strong is judged acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: A viable plan is workable and feasible, good enough to go ahead.

clue.text: Magic bird, the blackbird, nearly home

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the blackbird is dropped

parts.note: merle is an old or Scots word for the blackbird

explanation.surface: One bird turns into another by magic and almost reaches home.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on both senses: Merlin the wizard of Arthurian legend, and the merlin, a small falcon.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlin is both the legendary enchanter and a small falcon, so a magic figure that is also a bird.

clue.text: Food for Shakespeare at Stratford

indicators.note: the words that follow hold the answer within them, spanning a word break

parts.note: lies across the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Catering for Shakespeare in his home town.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is a casual slang plural for meals or grub, the stuff you put on a plate.

clue.text: Learner displayed in paper etc

indicators.note: displayed means laid out in a new arrangement, so the following letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A learner shown in a newspaper and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice is a trainee learning a trade under a skilled worker.

clue.text: Reverse of what the fairy-tale goose did, like the swan?

indicators.note: the reverse of a phrase is that phrase written backwards

parts.note: the goose that laid golden eggs: lay or, with or the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale question comparing the golden goose with a swan.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the swan is a royal bird: unmarked mute swans on open water belong to the Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Swans in Britain traditionally belong to the monarch, so a swan is a royal bird.

clue.text: Divorce scene is upset by a single blow

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: Reno, Nevada, was famous for quick divorces

explanation.surface: A divorce scene disrupted by one punch.
explanation.walkthrough: Reno in Nevada was once the world's quickie-divorce capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A oner is British slang for one decisive blow, a single knockout punch.

clue.text: 7 8's party in Grammar School not far away …

parts.note: by means near, close at hand

explanation.surface: A grammar school close at hand where Disraeli's party is in session.
explanation.definitionFit: Coningsby is one of Disraeli's political novels, published in 1844.

clue.text: … his story ends with unfinished account of 5 down doubled …

definitions.note: his story, a novel by Disraeli

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter is missing
the ends of a word are its first and last letters only

parts.note: the outside letters of the word
a bill is an account to pay

explanation.surface: Continuing the series: his story finishes with an incomplete record of the doubled nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Sybil's subtitle is The Two Nations: one nation (5 down) doubled. That tail is a hint, not wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybil, or The Two Nations is Disraeli's 1845 novel about rich and poor England.

clue.text: … his "2 crusade" starts taking South African party to the left

definitions.note: his novel subtitled The New Crusade

indicators.note: starts means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Disraeli's crusade novel set beside the ANC moving leftward.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 stands for 'new' from 2 down: Tancred is subtitled The New Crusade. 'to the left' looks like a reversal sign but means red.
explanation.definitionFit: Tancred, or The New Crusade is Disraeli's 1847 novel about a young nobleman's journey east.

clue.text: Lighter with its bow in front of the fleet

parts.note: its refers back to the first word of the clue, and a bow is a ship's front, so the opening letter

explanation.surface: A barge at the head of the navy's fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: Lighter suggests a flat barge among the ships, but it is a lamp; 'its bow' is the first letter of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp, something that gives light.
